paras: The posse shooting of an escaped convict near Roanoke took place in Virginia in May 1903, when a posse of 12 men pursued a Black man accused of fatally wounding a white man and shot him in the face with buckshot. The man escaped the posse but was later arrested at Roanoke by a policeman named Rigney, who stood to collect a $50 reward. The episode is known from a single unsourced paragraph in a Virginia weekly's column of state news.

The Highland Recorder described the man, whom it did not name, as a "notorious negro convict" who had been sentenced to the penitentiary three times and had escaped. At the time of the shooting he was working as a cook for a gang of railroad men.

According to the paper, the week before its report the man "fatally wounded a white man" and fled to the mountains; neither the wounded man nor the place of the shooting was named. A posse of 12 men followed him and "put a load of buckshot into his face," but he got away again. He was then captured in Roanoke by Policeman Rigney.

The paper said only that Rigney would be entitled to a $50 reward for the arrest. No report of the white man's death, a trial of the accused, or any inquiry into the posse's shooting was found in the coverage.

The only report ran on May 22, 1903, in "The Old Dominion," a column of Virginia news in the Highland Recorder of Monterey, Virginia, where it sat between a list of pensions and the death of a railway flagman. The item gave no source, stated the accusation against the man as fact, and reported the buckshot wound to his face without comment. No Black-press coverage of the episode was found.

record_check.record: A week-earlier shooting ... later recaptured in Roanoke.

info: The shooting of the white man and the posse's pursuit took place 'last week' relative to a weekly brief dated May 22, 1903, i.e. about mid-May 1903; the arrest date is not given.
The arrest was made at Roanoke; the place of the shooting and of the posse's pursuit is not stated beyond 'the mountains'.
One unnamed Black man, called a 'notorious negro convict' who had been sentenced to the penitentiary three times and had escaped; he was working as a cook for a gang of railroad men.
